title: The Grammar of Ornament
author: Owen Jones
notes: 100 chromolithographic plates surveying geometric ornament from Egyptian, Moorish, Persian, Celtic, and Renaissance traditions. Foundational reference for pattern design.

title: Owen Jones — Architectural Drawings and Color Studies
author: Owen Jones
notes: Working drawings and color studies by Owen Jones, including Alhambra documentation and pattern derivations.

title: Arabic Geometrical Pattern and Design
author: Jules Bourgoin
notes: 190 plates of Islamic geometric construction — girih tiles, star polygons, and their mathematical derivations from Bourgoin's survey of Cairo monuments.

title: Islamic Geometric Patterns
author: Various
notes: Geometric tilework, muqarnas, and arabesque patterns from mosques, madrasas, and palaces across the Islamic world.

title: Alhambra Tile Patterns
author: Unknown Nasrid artisans
notes: All 17 wallpaper symmetry groups are represented in Alhambra tilework. The most mathematically complete geometric programme in medieval architecture.

title: Geometric Patterns of the Alhambra — Detail Studies
author: Unknown Nasrid artisans
notes: Close-up documentation of individual panel patterns, zellij borders, and stucco geometric screens in the Alhambra.

title: Topkapi Palace — Islamic Art and Geometric Ornament
author: Various Ottoman artisans
notes: Iznik tile panels, geometric woodwork, and manuscript illumination from the imperial collections of the Topkapi Palace.

title: Mysterium Cosmographicum — Platonic Solid Nesting
author: Johannes Kepler
notes: Kepler's nested polyhedra model of the solar system — the five Platonic solids enclosing the six planetary orbits. The most celebrated diagram in early modern cosmology.

title: Harmonices Mundi — Geometric and Musical Diagrams
author: Johannes Kepler
notes: Diagrams of planetary harmonies, regular tilings, and the geometry of music from Kepler's masterwork on cosmic order.

title: Jain Cosmological Paintings
author: Various Jain manuscript painters
notes: Cosmological diagrams from Jain manuscripts including the Lokapurusha (cosmic man), Jambudvipa diagrams, and the concentrically mapped continents of Jain cosmology.

title: Lokapurusha — The Cosmic Man
author: Various Jain manuscript painters
notes: The Jain universe depicted as a human figure — the three realms (heavens, middle world, hells) mapped onto the cosmic body.

title: Jambudvipa — Jain World Map
author: Various Jain manuscript painters
notes: Circular cosmological maps of Jambudvipa, the central continent of Jain cosmology, with Mount Meru at center surrounded by concentric rings of landmass and ocean.

title: Buddhist Cosmological Diagrams
author: Various
notes: Painted diagrams of the Buddhist cosmos — Mount Meru, the four continents, the six realms of existence, and the thirty-three heavens.

title: Bhavachakra — Tibetan Wheel of Existence
author: Various Tibetan thangka painters
notes: The Wheel of Life (Bhavachakra) held by Yama, divided into the six realms of existence with the three poisons at the hub. A complete cosmological and soteriological diagram in one image.

title: Traiphum Phra Ruang — Thai Buddhist Cosmology
author: Various Thai manuscript painters
notes: Illustrated manuscripts of the Traiphum (Three Worlds cosmology), the foundational Thai Buddhist cosmological text. Vivid depictions of Mount Meru and the layered heavens.

title: Mappae Mundi — Medieval Cosmological World Maps
author: Various medieval cartographers
notes: T-O and other medieval cosmological world maps placing Jerusalem at center, paradise at the top, and organizing geography according to sacred geometry.

title: Ebstorf World Map (reconstruction)
author: Unknown, Ebstorf monastery
notes: The largest known medieval mappa mundi — 12 feet across, the world depicted as the body of Christ with Jerusalem at the navel. Destroyed 1943; known from 19th-century color facsimile.

title: Hindu Yantras — Devotional Geometric Diagrams
author: Various
notes: Sacred geometric diagrams used in Hindu worship — Sri Yantra, Kali Yantra, Navgraha Yantra, and others. Each yantra is a map of a deity's power reduced to pure geometry.

title: Sri Yantra
author: Various
notes: The most celebrated of Hindu geometric diagrams — nine interlocking triangles generating 43 smaller triangles around a central point (bindu), surrounded by lotus petals and a square gateway.

title: Celestial Globes
author: Various instrument makers
notes: Historical celestial globes mapping the constellations onto a sphere — the cosmos as a physical object. Includes Islamic, European, and East Asian examples.

title: Armillary Spheres
author: Various instrument makers
notes: Armillary spheres — nested metal rings representing the celestial equator, ecliptic, tropics, and meridians. Both scientific instruments and embodied cosmograms.

title: Gothic Rose Windows
author: Various medieval glaziers
notes: The great rose windows of Gothic cathedrals — Chartres, Notre-Dame de Paris, Reims — are the culmination of medieval geometric art, encoding cosmological order in stone and light.

title: Rose Windows of Notre-Dame de Paris
author: Unknown medieval glaziers
notes: The three rose windows of Notre-Dame — north, south, and west — each a different geometric programme radiating from a central point.

title: Vitruvian Man
author: Leonardo da Vinci
notes: Leonardo's diagram of ideal human proportions inscribed in circle and square — the image of man as the measure of all things and the link between earthly and cosmic geometry.

title: Leonardo da Vinci — Polyhedra Illustrations for De Divina Proportione
author: Leonardo da Vinci
notes: Leonardo's 60 skeletal polyhedra drawn for Luca Pacioli's De Divina Proportione — the Platonic and Archimedean solids rendered in three dimensions for the first time.

title: De Divina Proportione — Illustrations
author: Luca Pacioli / Leonardo da Vinci
notes: Pacioli's treatise on the golden ratio with Leonardo's polyhedra illustrations. The foundational text on mathematical proportion in art and architecture.

title: Euclid's Elements — Historical Illustrations
author: Various
notes: Geometric diagrams from early printed and manuscript editions of Euclid's Elements — the diagrams that defined visual mathematical reasoning for two millennia.

title: Book of Kells — Illuminated Pages
author: Unknown Insular monks
notes: The supreme achievement of Insular art — interlace knotwork, zoomorphic panels, and carpet pages of extraordinary geometric complexity. Trinity College Dublin MS 58.

title: Lindisfarne Gospels — Carpet Pages
author: Eadfrith, Bishop of Lindisfarne
notes: Celtic knotwork carpet pages from the Lindisfarne Gospels — interlace patterns of staggering precision drawn without a compass, each panel a meditation in geometric form.

title: Penrose Tilings
author: Roger Penrose
notes: Aperiodic tilings by Roger Penrose demonstrating quasicrystalline fivefold symmetry — patterns with local order but no global periodicity, later found in medieval Islamic geometric art.

title: Platonic Solids — Historical Illustrations and Models
author: Various
notes: Visual history of the five Platonic solids from Euclid through Kepler — drawings, woodcuts, physical models, and symbolic diagrams from mathematical and cosmological traditions.

title: Metatron's Cube and Flower of Life
author: Various
notes: Sacred geometry diagrams from Western esoteric tradition — the Flower of Life, Fruit of Life, and Metatron's Cube, which contains all five Platonic solids in projection.

title: Mandalas — Cosmological Diagrams from Asian Traditions
author: Various
notes: Sacred circles from Buddhist, Hindu, and Jain traditions — Kalachakra, Womb World, Diamond World, and devotional mandalas of individual deities.

title: Kalachakra Mandala
author: Various Tibetan painters
notes: The Wheel of Time mandala — 722 deities arranged in concentric geometric palaces. The most complex of Vajrayana cosmological diagrams, used in Dalai Lama initiation ceremonies.

title: Pre-modern Cosmological Diagrams
author: Various
notes: Cosmological schematics from medieval and Renaissance European sources — sphere diagrams, elemental wheels, and geometric representations of the Ptolemaic cosmos.

title: Labyrinths — Sacred Ground Plans
author: Various
notes: Historical labyrinth designs from Cretan coins through Chartres Cathedral — the single-path labyrinth as cosmological symbol, initiation device, and meditation tool.

title: Chartres Labyrinth
author: Unknown medieval mason
notes: The eleven-circuit labyrinth inlaid in the nave floor of Chartres Cathedral — 261.5 feet to walk, the same diameter as the west rose window directly above it.

title: Islamic Calligraphy as Geometric Art
author: Various calligraphers
notes: Kufic, Thuluth, and other scripts structured by geometric grids — the word as sacred geometry. Includes square Kufic and mirrored bismillah compositions.

title: Muqarnas — Islamic Geometric Vaulting
author: Various Islamic architects and craftsmen
notes: Stalactite vaulting from mosques and palaces — Alhambra, Imam Mosque Isfahan, Nasir al-Mulk. Three-dimensional geometric crystallography in stone and plaster.

title: Girih Tiles — Islamic Quasi-Crystalline Geometry
author: Various Islamic craftsmen
notes: The five girih tiles found at the Darb-i Imam shrine (1453) generate quasi-crystalline Penrose-type patterns — 500 years before Penrose's mathematical discovery.

title: Geometric Art — Survey
author: Various
notes: Survey category for geometric art across cultures and periods — useful as a fallback discovery category.
